case_name: United States v. Colorado County, Runnels County, Smith County, and Upton County (Texas) — Election Website Accessibility
court: DOJ settlement agreements — U.S. District Court, Eastern/Northern/Southern/Western Districts of Texas
docket: Multiple — see DOJ press release (archived June 2024)
claim_type: County election websites violated ADA by discriminating against individuals with vision or manual disabilities
outcome: Settlement agreements requiring all four counties to make election websites accessible to people with disabilities under Title II of the ADA

sources.name: DOJ — Justice Department Secures Agreements with Texas Counties (June 2024)

summary_one_line: DOJ in 2024 required four Texas counties to make election websites accessible under Title II of the ADA — shows DOJ enforcement extends to government sites, not just commercial businesses.
notes: Included as a supplementary government sector case showing breadth of DOJ enforcement. Primary relevance to report: any public-facing digital property — government or commercial — is subject to ADA enforcement. Note this is Title II (government) not Title III (commercial) — keep the legal distinction clear in the report.
